$comment: Every number and label SYNAPSE shows must trace back to an id in this file, or be marked as an assumption. docs/sources.md is generated from it (make sources).

challenge.title: Space Apps 2026 challenge: Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions
findings: Asks for a visual tool so astronauts can assess their health indicators and get guidance
Accepts keyboard, mouse or camera input

hrp-hazards.title: NASA HRP: 5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight
findings: Five hazards: Space Radiation; Isolation and Confinement; Distance from Earth; Gravity Fields; Hostile/Closed Environments
On Mars, astronauts would live in 3/8 of Earth's gravity for up to two years; a Mars trip lasts about three years
Hostile/Closed Environments covers habitability: temperature, pressure, lighting, noise, microbes, immune responses
No numeric thresholds

hrp-risks.title: NASA HRP: Risks of Human Spaceflight
findings: 17 official risks in three groups: human physiology, behavioral performance and human factors, space radiation
None of them is about cabin CO2
No numeric thresholds

hrp-ongoing-research.title: NASA HRP: Ongoing HRP Research
findings: ARCHeR tracked the Artemis II crew's wellbeing, activity and sleep with a wrist actigraphy device (as summarized in the plan)

csa-radiation.title: CSA: Monitoring radiation for astronaut health (2026-02-26)
findings: CANS is a compact, autonomous instrument to measure neutron radiation exposure in space
Neutron radiation contributes about 30% of total radiation on the ISS
No dose dataset

csa-why-science.title: CSA: Why do we conduct science experiments in space?
findings: Context for the Science Contribution Score and the Earth-use closing of the pitch

jones-2022-sleep.title: Jones et al. (2022), Sleep deficiency in spaceflight is associated with degraded neurobehavioral functions and elevated stress in astronauts on six-month missions aboard the ISS, Sleep
findings: 24 astronauts on 6-month ISS missions, Reaction Self Test with PVT-B
Astronauts reported sleeping 6.5 h on average in flight
Sleep under 6 h was associated with slower psychomotor response, higher stress and workload
Sleep under 5 h was associated with negative somatic states
Sleep was self-reported

flynn-evans-2016-circadian.title: Flynn-Evans et al. (2016), Circadian misalignment affects sleep and medication use before and during spaceflight, npj Microgravity
findings: Actigraphy from 21 ISS missions, 3,248 days of spaceflight
Sleep averaged 6.4 h when aligned with circadian timing and 5.4 h when misaligned

basner-2011-pvtb.title: Basner, Mollicone & Dinges (2011), Validity and sensitivity of a brief psychomotor vigilance test (PVT-B) to total and partial sleep deprivation, Acta Astronautica
findings: 3-minute PVT-B
Lapse threshold lowered from 500 ms to 355 ms, chosen so that PVT-B lapse frequency matched the 10-minute PVT; measured on the handheld PVT-192 device
Inter-stimulus interval 1-4 s, including 1 s of reaction-time feedback (Section 2.2, checked against the original on 2026-11-14)
A response with no stimulus or a reaction under 100 ms is a false start; 30 s without a response counts as a lapse with a 30 s reaction time
Metrics are response speed (1/RT), lapses, fastest and slowest 10% and a performance score; a mean reaction time in ms is not one of them
A 3-minute test sampled 62.3 stimuli on average; lapse frequency was 5.3% across the study
Only Methods and part of Results were read verbatim; Discussion and Conclusions are unverified

fmcsa-1998-perclos.title: FMCSA Technology Division (1998), PERCLOS: A Valid Psychophysiological Measure of Alertness As Assessed by Psychomotor Vigilance, tech brief FHWA-MCRT-98-006
findings: PERCLOS: proportion of time in a minute that the eyes are at least 80 percent closed (Wierwille et al., 1994)
Reflects slow eyelid closures, not blinks

dinges-1998-ocular.title: Dinges, Mallis, Maislin & Powell (1998), Evaluation of techniques for ocular measurement as an index of fatigue and as the basis for alertness management, NHTSA DOT HS 808 762
findings: PERCLOS validated against PVT lapses under sleep deprivation

soukupova-2016-ear.title: Soukupová & Čech (2016), Real-Time Eye Blink Detection using Facial Landmarks, 21st Computer Vision Winter Workshop
findings: EAR = (|p2-p6| + |p3-p5|) / (2|p1-p4|) from six eye landmarks
A fixed 0.2 threshold is only a baseline; an SVM over a temporal window detects blinks, since blink patterns differ per person

nasa-pvt-iss.title: Psychomotor Vigilance Test (PVT) on ISS (data.nasa.gov)
findings: Was the design reference for the PVT-B
Returns 404 as of 2026-11-14: the dataset is no longer on data.nasa.gov

nasa-standard-measures.title: NASA Spaceflight Standard Measures (NTRS)
findings: Raw per-astronaut data is not public; HRP shares it only through data sharing agreements

asrs-report-sets.title: NASA ASRS Database Report Sets
findings: Two fatigue sets of 50 reports each: air carrier (FAR 121) and commuter/corporate crews
Fatigue co-occurs with lost situational awareness in 65 of 100 reports; 46 happen in approach, descent or landing; 82 involve a procedural deviation (research/nasa-data/findings/asrs.txt)
Voluntary, uncorroborated reports: counts describe the sample, not how often anything happens
Source for the forensic intro script

uta-rldd.title: UTA Real-Life Drowsiness Dataset
findings: About 30 h of webcam/phone video from 60 people: alert, low vigilance, drowsy
Main training set for the fatigue model
Paper: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1904.07312

drozy.title: DROZY drowsiness database (University of Liege)
findings: 14 subjects, 28-30 h awake; face video, polysomnography, KSS and PVT synchronized

yawdd.title: YawDD yawning detection dataset
findings: Videos of drivers talking, singing and yawning; validates yawn detection

mrl-eye.title: MRL Eye Dataset
findings: 84,898 infrared eye images, open or closed; optional check of the eye-closed threshold

osdr-inspiration4.title: Overbey et al. (2024), Inspiration4 data access through the NASA Open Science Data Repository, npj Microgravity
findings: First open-access human dataset from a commercial spaceflight: 4 civilian crew, 3-day orbital mission (2021)
Processed data are public; raw genetic data need an approved application

osdr-osd-569.title: NASA OSDR OSD-569: Whole blood measurements from the SpaceX Inspiration4 mission (includes the complete blood count)
findings: Complete blood count for 4 crew at 7 draws (L-92, L-44, L-3, R+1, R+45, R+82, R+194) with the lab's reference ranges

Day after landing, in all 4 crew: white cells about -20%, monocyte share about +26%, red cell size (MCV) about -4%; the white-cell and monocyte shifts persist to R+194, so they are not clearly flight effects (research/nasa-data/findings/labs.txt)

osdr-osd-575.title: NASA OSDR OSD-575: Inspiration4 serum: comprehensive metabolic panel and immune/cardiovascular multiplex panels
findings: Lab reference ranges: glucose 65-99 mg/dL, potassium 3.5-5.3 mmol/L, sodium 135-146 mmol/L, calcium 8.6-10.2 mg/dL
Day after landing, in all 4 crew: glucose about +23% (back to baseline later; fasting state unknown), bicarbonate (CO2) about -4%
The multiplex panel's L-44 draw reads about 10x lower in all crew and some values sit at the assay ceiling: treat that panel's trends as unreliable

trudel-2022-hemolysis.title: Trudel et al. (2022), Hemolysis contributes to anemia during long-duration space flight, Nature Medicine
findings: 14 astronauts on 6-month missions destroyed 54% more red blood cells than on Earth
Space anemia resolved within 3-4 months back on Earth; destruction was still 30% above preflight a year later
